$comment: The eight things a country can lead on. A lens is not a tag applied to everything — every country in the set has all twenty-seven categories written up, so filtering on those would light the whole map and tell a traveller nothing. A lens is what a country declares in its own `calls`, which is editorial and deliberately short: Uganda calls wildlife and culture, and does not call coast, even though it has lakes. `categories` is the other direction — which of the twenty-seven write-ups belong to this lens, so opening a country under a lens leads with the right places. There were six, and between them they described the continent's landscape: wildlife, culture, coast, heritage, mountains, food. That is a stereotype of African tourism rather than an account of it — safari, nature, beach, village. `cities` is now a lens of its own rather than a category buried inside heritage; `mountains` widens into `nature`; `heritage` narrows to `history` once cities and architecture leave it; and `adventure` comes out of the old mountains lens to stand on its own, which also fixes a picker that offered `adventure` and `rainforest` as choices when neither was a lens and both therefore filtered to nothing.

cities.title: Cities
cities.line: Where the continent is loudest, newest and most itself.
cities.label: Cities
cities.examples: Lagos, Cape Town, Marrakech, Nairobi, Dakar, Accra
cities.filterline: If the cities are what brought you here
cities.feel: Hear a city come alive after dark, and realise it was waiting all day.
cities.photo_alt: Nairobi after dark from above, lit avenues running back between towers to the horizon

wildlife.title: Wildlife
wildlife.line: Where the animals are the reason you came.
wildlife.label: Wildlife
wildlife.examples: Gorillas, elephants, lions, giraffes, chimpanzees, the great migration
wildlife.filterline: If wildlife is what brought you here
wildlife.feel: Look across a savanna and see nothing between you and the horizon.
wildlife.photo_alt: A line of elephants walking across open dry grassland with nothing between them and a flat horizon

culture.title: Culture
culture.line: Kingdoms, languages, festivals and the people who keep them.
culture.label: People & culture
culture.examples: Kingdoms, markets, music, dance, craft, living traditions
culture.filterline: If you came to meet people
culture.feel: Sit down somewhere a kingdom still holds court, and it is not a museum.
culture.photo_alt: A bronze caster at work on the craft street at Foumban, seat of the Bamoun kings

coast.title: Coast
coast.line: Atlantic, Indian Ocean, Mediterranean, and the lakes big enough to have surf.
coast.label: Coast & islands
coast.filterline: If you came for the water
coast.feel: Swim in water clear enough to lose the horizon in.
coast.photo_alt: A ngalawa outrigger canoe drawn up on a shore of clear shallow water on the Swahili coast

nature.title: Nature
nature.line: Mountain, forest, desert and the country between them.
nature.label: Nature
nature.examples: Kilimanjaro, Korup, the Rwenzori, the Atlas, the Namib
nature.filterline: If you came for the country itself
nature.feel: Wake up above the clouds, on a mountain that stands alone over the plain.
nature.photo_alt: The snow-capped summit of Kilimanjaro above a band of cloud, standing alone over a plain of acacia and elephants

food.title: Food
food.line: What a country actually eats, not what it serves tourists.
food.label: African food
food.examples: Street food, markets, coastal cuisine, home cooking, coffee
food.feel: Eat what a country actually eats, at the hour it actually eats it.
food.photo_alt: Stalls of fruit and vegetables piled under a market roof, shoppers moving between them

history.title: History
history.line: Ruins, empires, and the places that remember what happened on them.
history.label: History
history.examples: Forts, palaces, ancient cities, rock churches, sacred places
history.filterline: If you came for what was here before you
history.feel: Stand on ground that remembers, and has done for four thousand years.
history.photo_alt: The Great Pyramid and the Pyramid of Khafre at Giza from the causeway at dusk, stone that has stood for four and a half thousand years

adventure.title: Adventure
adventure.line: Long roads, thin air, white water and the walk in.
adventure.label: Adventure
adventure.examples: Gravel roads, the Nile at Jinja, the falls from both sides, the long traverse
adventure.filterline: If you came to go a long way
adventure.feel: Cross a desert before sunrise, because by ten it will not let you.
adventure.photo_alt: A camp of white canvas tents on open sand with the sun just clear of the dunes behind them

$feel_note: `feel` is the one field in this file that is written rather than derived, and
it is the only place on the homepage where that is true of a whole section.
The page had an answer to `what is Africa` — twenty-two countries, twenty-seven
categories, five regions, all of it counted off disk — and no answer at all to
`why would I go`. A visitor who does not yet want to travel has no use for a
comparison engine. So the section under the hero asks what you want to feel
before it offers anything to browse, and these are the eight answers.
The sentence is authored. What sits under it is not: the count and the
countries come from which countries actually call this lens in their own
`calls`, so a line that promises something is printed next to the places it is
true of. A lens no country calls is not offered — a feeling with nowhere to
have it is the one kind of copy this site cannot print.
